title: Terraform telemetry module: canary-safe upgrades, probe-driven health checks, and log-forwarding policies
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description:
Scope: Build a reusable Terraform module that provisions an opinionated observability stack for VPC/private deployments: Prometheus (server + Alertmanager), Grafana (config + datasource provisioning), OpenTelemetry Collector (OTel) as the ingestion/transform layer, and a log shipper (Fluent Bit) that forwards to S3 or customer-managed logging endpoints. The module must be compatible with Redwood Private (VPC) deployments and support upgrade safety via canary releases, automated health probes, and pre/post hooks for graceful upgrades.

Goals:
- Single Terraform module (module inputs with fine-grained feature flags) to deploy the above stack per deployment cell.
- Canary upgrade strategy: create canary replicas and validate telemetry parity before shifting traffic.
- Health checks: readiness/liveness and metric-driven acceptance checks (e.g., OTel scrape success, log-forwarding throughput, Prometheus target health).
- Plan-only and drift detection pipelines: terraform plan checks in CI and daily drift scans.
- Secure defaults: KMS support for secrets, least-privileged IAM roles, RBAC for Grafana provisioning API.
- Observability of the observability stack: export module-level metrics to the cell-level Prom and wire Dashboards for launch playbooks.

Constraints and decisions:
- Protocol: OTLP (gRPC) selected as the canonical ingestion protocol for consistency with hosted agents and lower CPU compared to HTTP.
- Storage: module will support either managed S3/GCS sinks or customer-provided endpoints; retention/compaction left to customer config.
- Upgrade model: immutable canary-style deployments (blue/green-style for collector + fluent-bit daemonset updates) with configurable canary size and verification steps.

Acceptance criteria:
- Terraform module deploys stack into a fresh test VPC (CI cluster) via a dedicated CI pipeline and passes e2e smoke tests.
- Canary upgrade executed in CI: new collector image is rolled into 10% of replicas; system verifies metric parity and log continuity for 10 minutes before promoting.
- Health checks: module exposes k8s readiness probes and a separate 'module-health' Prometheus exporter that computes a single boolean health metric for alerting.
- Docs: README with example usage, upgrade runbook, and a migration guide for existing manual installs.
- Security: secrets are stored in KMS-backed SSM/Secrets Manager; Terraform plan fails on unsecured secrets or open network rules.

Deliverables:
- terraform/modules/observability (module entrypoint and examples)
- CI pipelines: plan, apply with manual approval for prod cells, canary-runner job to validate upgrades
- Test harness: lightweight k3s kind job used in CI to smoke test installs and upgrades
- Grafana provisioning templates and sample dashboards for module-level SLOs
- Runbook and upgrade checklist uploaded to Confluence
acceptance_criteria:
1) Runs terraform plan and apply against a test VPC without manual patching.
2) Canary upgrade path: deploy new collector image to 10% of collector pods, validate (a) no error-rate spike in collector logs, (b) Prometheus target health remains >= 95%, (c) log-forwarder shows no drops for 5m.
3) Module exports a single 'observability_module_healthy' metric used by cell-level Alerting rules.
4) README contains example usage for S3 sink + customer endpoint and a migration path for existing clusters.
5) Security gates: CI must fail if secrets are stored unencrypted or if IAM policy contains wildcard '*' privileges.

2026-03-11 - Marco L: Reviewed and suggested adding a plan-only 'preflight' pipeline and a daily drift scan job. Also suggested adding lifecycle.ignore_changes for autoscaler-managed fields to avoid noisy diffs.

2026-03-12 - Priya Santos (SRE): Asked for metric-driven canary validation (not just pod health). Recommended an export of per-upgrade test metrics to a dedicated Prometheus job. Will add an alert if parity test fails. See design notes: https://drive.redwood.ai/obs-module/canary-playbook.md

2026-03-13 - Marco L: Opening draft PR https://github.com/redwood-inference/terraform-modules/pull/789. Implemented initial module inputs, example usage, and k3s CI job. Raised a blocker: Fluent Bit config templating needs sanitization for customer endpoints (potential header injection).

2026-03-13 - Security review (security-team): Security review requested. Action: add KMS integration doc and require terraform variable enforce_kms=true for prod. Marked security_review_required=true in ticket.
2026-03-13 - QA: Added test matrix comment: must validate both S3 and HTTPS sinks, and with/without auth. CI job added to test HTTPS sink with ephemeral certificate issuance.
notes:
Implementation notes: avoid mutable in-place upgrades for collector when enabling new pipelines; instead create new Deployment/StatefulSet for canary and swap service DNS. Use Terraform null_resource with local-exec for running lightweight validation scripts (curl to /metrics, compare time-series). Provide example policy docs for least-privilege IAM roles. Add module variable 'canary_validation_queries' to accept list of PromQL used by the CI runner.

Open questions:
- How to handle existing dashboards for customers that have custom Grafana provisioning? Plan to support 'provisioning = false' and leave Grafana untouched.
- Rollback strategy: module will provide a safe 'abort' hook to reverse deployment; but operator rollback playbook still required.

Next steps:
- Finish PR and include unit tests for TF 1.6 compatibility.
- Add digest-based image pinning and support for curated runtime images from our internal registry.
- Schedule security review meeting with security-team to close KMS/IAM items.
